items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb’s Cancer Drug Just Doubled Survival Time Without Progression — Here’s Why It Matters

AWS and Azure are experiencing strong revenue growth and profitability, with AWS at $169 billion annualized revenue and Azure at $100 billion. Microsoft is highlighted as having additional growth potential through its Copilot AI software ecosystem integrated with Azure.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reaffirms His $4 Trillion Projection for AI Spending. Here's Why That Makes Nvidia a Screaming Buy Now.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reaffirmed his projection that global data center capital expenditures will reach $3-4 trillion annually by 2030, up from an estimated $1 trillion this year. If Nvidia maintains its market share as the AI infrastructure market grows, the company could see revenue triple to quadruple to $1.2-1.6 trillion annually, potentially resulting in a market cap of $18-24 trillion compared to its current $5.4 trillion valuation.

items.title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Revenue Trends to Help Investors Weigh Which Artificial Intelligence Stock to Buy
items.summary: SK Hynix has dramatically surpassed Intel in revenue growth over the past two years, reaching $52.6 billion in Q2 2026 compared to Intel's $16.1 billion, driven by massive demand for advanced memory semiconductors. While SK Hynix achieved historic profitability with a 76% operating margin, Intel is attempting a turnaround under new CEO Lip-Bu Tan, with Q2 2026 marking its highest quarterly sales in two years. The key question for investors is whether SK Hynix's exceptional growth will sustain or face margin pressure as manufacturing capacity expands.

items.title: Why Comfort Systems Plunged Today
items.summary: Comfort Systems stock fell 9.36% despite beating revenue and earnings estimates with 53.7% revenue growth and 68.6% EPS growth to $13.91. The decline was driven by CFO Bill George's retirement announcement and broader 'sell the news' sentiment among AI-related stocks, as investors worry about the sustainability of the AI data center build-out beyond 2027. The stock now trades at a reasonable 19.4x forward 2027 earnings, down 38% from its June high.

items.title: Intel Stock Has Moved an Average of 16% the Day After Its Last 3 Reports. Should You Buy Before the Next One?
items.summary: Intel stock has experienced volatile swings averaging 16% the day after its last three earnings reports, despite beating forecasts each time. The key driver of stock movement appears to be forward guidance rather than quarterly results. While Intel topped revenue expectations in April (stock surged 24%) and July (stock fell 8% despite strong results), the pattern suggests investors focus on sequential growth rates and capital spending outlooks. With the next earnings report due October 29, the fourth-quarter guidance—particularly regarding supply growth and revenue trajectory—will likely be the critical factor determining stock direction.

items.title: Bloom Energy Stock Sinks Despite Record Revenue and a Stellar Outlook. Is It Time to Buy?

items.title: Not So Fast! One Warren Buffett's Core Positions at Berkshire Hathaway May Not Get the Heave-Ho by Successor Greg Abel After All.

items.title: If You Invested $100 a Month in This High-Yield Dividend Stock, Here's the Dividend Income It Produced Over 10 Years
items.summary: Altria Group (MO), the largest U.S. tobacco company, demonstrated strong dividend performance over the past decade. A $100 monthly investment ($12,000 principal) generated approximately $4,800 in dividends while growing to $13,800. With a 5.9% forward dividend yield and 57 consecutive years of annual dividend increases (Dividend King status), Altria maintains a cheap valuation at 13x forward earnings. The company offsets declining smoking rates through price increases, cost cuts, share buybacks, and expansion into smoke-free products, with expectations to generate $5 billion in smoke-free revenue by 2028.

items.title: The Trillion-Dollar AI Bet: What It Means for Hyperscaler Investors
items.summary: The five major hyperscalers (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Oracle) are projected to spend nearly $780 billion on AI capital expenditures in 2026, escalating to over $1 trillion annually from 2027-2030. While this massive investment presents significant financial risks—including soaring debt levels and negative free cash flow—the long-term payoff remains uncertain. Success requires the AI economy to generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031, with most value potentially shifting away from hyperscalers toward companies offering differentiated end-customer products.

Bending Spoons has a strong track record of improving acquired companies' operations and achieving high returns on capital, though it faces risks from significant leverage and capital deployment challenges.

items.title: Lockheed Martin's $230 Billion Backlog, Explained
items.summary: Lockheed Martin's backlog has grown to $230 billion, representing 2.8 times its estimated 2026 revenue and signaling strong future growth. The majority of backlog growth is concentrated in the high-margin Missiles and Fire Control segment, driven by orders for mature systems like THAAD and PAC-3 interceptors. This represents lower-risk, potentially higher-margin business compared to previous years, supporting a positive investment outlook.

items.title: Here's How Microsoft's $175 Billion in Capital Expenditures Is Hurting Its Business
items.summary: Microsoft is investing $175 billion in data center capital expenditures to support AI and cloud computing growth. However, the article argues this heavy spending on lower-margin Azure cloud business may pressure overall operating margins, as Azure's margins likely align with competitors AWS (36-39%) rather than Microsoft's higher overall margins (45%). While necessary to compete, this growth may slow profit expansion relative to revenue growth, making Amazon and Alphabet more attractive AI investments.

items.title: Competing for Eyeballs: Can Pinterest Stage a Comeback or Will Reddit Run Away With the AI Win?

items.title: Johnson & Johnson: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year sales outlook after Q3 2026 operational revenue grew 6%, putting the company on track to exceed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time. Strong pharmaceutical demand, particularly in cancer treatments, drove performance. However, the medical device segment faced headwinds with only 2.5% growth due to Middle East disruptions and China's bulk-buying program. Management plans to restore momentum through new product launches and is leaning toward spinning off its DePuy Synthes orthopedics subsidiary by mid-2027.

items.title: Why Applied Optoelectronics Stock Plummeted This Week
items.summary: Applied Optoelectronics stock fell 23.6% this week after Broadcom CEO warned of capital constraints that could slow AI infrastructure spending. The optical component maker, which relies heavily on data center customers for 800G transceivers, faces headwinds from funding concerns among major cloud providers. The stock has declined 64.2% from its 52-week high, compounded by recent shareholder dilution from a $600 million equity offering.

items.title: CFG Stock Up as Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on NII Growth, Dividend Hiked
items.summary: Citizens Financial Group reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.41, beating estimates of $1.38, with a 34% year-over-year increase. The company benefited from 13% NII growth to $1.68 billion and a 19 basis point NIM expansion to 3.19%. CFG raised its dividend by 13% to 52 cents and expanded share repurchase authorization to $1.95 billion. However, elevated expenses and a weaker capital position remain headwinds.

items.title: M&T Bank Q3 Earnings Beat on Higher NII, Stock Dips on Cost Woes
items.summary: M&T Bank (MTB) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $5.08, beating estimates of $4.98, with net interest income rising 1.8% year-over-year to $1.81 billion and loans growing 1.6% sequentially. However, shares fell 1.2% as non-interest income declined 1.2% and expenses rose 2.2%, while deposits fell sequentially. The company projects Q4 NII of $1.83-$1.85 billion with a mid-3.60% net interest margin.

items.title: Vaso Stock Surges 149% in a Year: What's Behind the Rally?
items.summary: Vaso Corporation (VASO) has gained 149% over the past year, significantly outperforming its industry peers and the S&P 500. The healthcare-focused company reported improved Q2 2026 results with higher revenues and profitability, driven by growth in professional sales services and medical device segments. Following the divestiture of its IT services business, VASO is streamlining operations and strengthening its focus on healthcare. However, the company faces challenges including heavy dependence on GE HealthCare and ongoing profitability pressures in its proprietary medical products division.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase reported Q3 2026 net income of $15.3 billion on $50.9 billion revenue. The bank is prioritizing organic growth over share buybacks, deploying AI tools internally while restricting external agents for security, and projects $107 billion in 2027 net interest income. Management highlights consumer resilience and steady execution across market conditions.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased AppLovin securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Goldman Sachs: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Goldman Sachs reported Q3 2026 net revenues of $18.7 billion, with financing activities representing over 40% of trading revenues. The bank is strengthening earnings stability through recurring revenue streams in asset management, expense discipline, and strategic growth in AI data center infrastructure financing. Management expects accelerating corporate dealmaking as clients modernize operations and seek capital for infrastructure buildouts.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Urges Investors of GoDaddy Inc. (NYSE: GDDY) to Seek a Leadership Role Before October 20, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a class action lawsuit against GoDaddy Inc. (NYSE: GDDY) on behalf of investors who purchased stock between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that GoDaddy misled investors about its customer acquisition strategy by failing to disclose a $4.99 promotional offer for one-year dotcom domains, which contradicted claims about focusing on high-intent customers. The undisclosed promotion led to shorter-term contracts and reduced bookings growth, causing the stock to drop 14.28% on February 25, 2026 when the company revealed the decelerated bookings growth and promotional strategy.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges GoDaddy Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against GoDaddy Inc. alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that GoDaddy made false statements about its customer strategy, which prioritized short-term contracts over sustainable growth, resulting in materially decelerated bookings growth. Investors who purchased GoDaddy securities between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026 are encouraged to join the case.

items.title: Is COST a Buy as Strong Growth Meets a Premium Earnings Valuation?
items.summary: Costco projects fiscal 2027 revenues to grow 8.4% to $328.53 billion with 11% earnings growth, supported by 84.1 million memberships and 20%+ digital sales growth. However, the stock trades at 42.3X forward earnings—well above industry and market averages—creating execution risk. Margin pressures from labor costs, tariffs, and commodity inflation further complicate the outlook, warranting a cautious stance despite strong operational fundamentals.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Warns That Inflation, Rising Asset Prices, and More "Continue to Shift Under the Surface."
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase's Q3 earnings missed expectations with EPS of $5.57 versus $5.93 expected and revenue of $50.17 billion versus $51.23 billion anticipated. CEO Jamie Dimon warned of multiple economic headwinds including large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates, and geopolitical tensions that could impact the bank and economy. While market activity remains strong, particularly from AI spending, Dimon noted activity was already moderating in Q3.

items.title: IBKR Q3 Earnings Match Estimates on Higher Revenues, Dividend Hiked
items.summary: Interactive Brokers (IBKR) delivered Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of 67 cents, matching estimates, with revenues climbing 16.3% to $1.87B. Net interest income grew 19.3% to $1.15B, while customer accounts surged 35.1% to 5.58M. The company increased its quarterly dividend by 71.4%. However, expenses rose 21.9% and pretax margin slipped to 78%, presenting some headwinds despite strong overall performance.

items.title: S&P 500 Stock Casey's Dropped 30% in Its Biggest Pullback Since the Great Recession -- Here's Why I'm Buying More
items.summary: Casey's General Stores stock has fallen 30% from its June all-time high, driven by disappointing earnings guidance, slowing inside sales growth, and concerns about consumer financial stress. However, the author views this as a buying opportunity, as the company's valuation has normalized from 50x to 31x earnings. With a strong acquisition strategy, 25 years of same-store sales growth, and plans to add 400+ stores by 2029, Casey's remains well-positioned for long-term growth despite near-term headwinds.

items.title: THE BUSINESS COUNCIL ANNOUNCES LEADERSHIP TRANSITION AS GOLDMAN SACHS CEO DAVID SOLOMON TAKES THE HELM
items.summary: David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, has been named the new chair of The Business Council, succeeding Brian Cornell of Target Corporation. Solomon will lead the organization during a pivotal period marked by AI advancement and complex global economic challenges. The Business Council, established in 1933, serves as a forum for world-leading CEOs to collaborate on business solutions.

items.title: TFC Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Securities Losses, Higher Costs Hurt
items.summary: Truist Financial's Q3 2026 adjusted EPS rose 11.5% year-over-year to $1.16 but missed consensus estimates by one cent due to $1.4 billion in securities losses and higher non-interest expenses. The company benefited from record wealth management income and 3.6% deposit growth, but profitability metrics weakened significantly. Management projects Q4 revenues of $5.35B with NII of $3.65-$3.70B.

items.title: APP Investors Have Opportunity to Lead AppLovin Corporation Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
items.summary: Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP announced a class action lawsuit against AppLovin Corporation for securities violations. The lawsuit alleges the company made false and misleading statements about its generative AI video tool, overstated AI model improvements, and exaggerated benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' AI system. The class period spans February 12, 2026 to August 5, 2026, with a deadline of November 16, 2026 for investors to participate.

items.title: Equifax Gears Up to Post Q3 Earnings: What Should Investors Know?
items.summary: Equifax is expected to report Q3 2026 results on October 20 with revenues projected to rise 9.6% year-over-year to $1.7B and EPS growth of 7.8% to $2.20. The company's Workforce Solutions segment is anticipated to grow 12%, while USIS and International segments are expected to show solid margin expansion. However, the Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat due to a negative Earnings ESP of -0.59% and a Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell).

items.title: ASML Can't Keep Up With 2027 or 2028 Demand. Is It the Best AI Stock to Buy Now?
items.summary: ASML reported record Q3 2026 results with 11.7 billion euros in revenue and 57.5% gross margins, beating guidance. The semiconductor equipment maker faces supply constraints as demand for AI chip manufacturing equipment outpaces production capacity. Management indicated that even planned 30% production increases for 2027-2028 may be insufficient to meet customer demand, signaling strong pricing power and long-term growth potential in EUV lithography systems.

items.title: Western Digital Pre-Q1 Earnings: Buy the Stock Now or Wait for Results?
items.summary: Western Digital is set to report Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings on October 22, projecting 45% YoY revenue growth to $4.1 billion driven by AI-driven storage demand and high-capacity HDD launches. The company has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with 0.00% Earnings ESP, suggesting no earnings beat expected. While strong fundamentals and AI/cloud exposure are positive, intense competition, execution risks, and elevated valuations present concerns.

items.title: PLD Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Rent Recovery and Rate Risks
items.summary: Prologis (PLD) lifted its 2026 cash same-store NOI growth guidance to 7-7.5% as U.S. industrial vacancy tightened to 7.1% and rents rose for the third consecutive quarter. The company outlined a 5.8-gigawatt data center pipeline and expects the SEGRO acquisition to close in H1 2027. However, higher interest rates pose risks to property transactions and valuations, and the Zacks Rank reflects unfavorable earnings estimate revisions.

items.title: IBKR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Trading and Growth Plans
items.summary: Interactive Brokers (IBKR) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.67 per share, beating revenue expectations at $1.87 billion. The company saw customer accounts grow 35% to 5.58 million and net interest income climb 19% to $1.15 billion. IBKR expanded autonomous AI trading capabilities, broadened global market access, and raised its quarterly dividend to 15 cents from 8.75 cents, reflecting confidence in its capital position. However, daily average revenue trades declined 11% sequentially, attributed partly to delayed IPOs.

items.title: BNY Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and AI Push
items.summary: Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) raised its 2026 operating leverage outlook to nearly 500 basis points with projected revenue growth of 12-13%, driven by strong Securities Services growth (up 15%), net interest income growth (up 15%), and deployment of over 400 AI solutions. The company beat earnings estimates with $5.68B in revenue and $2.37 EPS, while expanding digital asset capabilities and maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

items.title: Starbucks Stock Gains 15% YTD: Can Its Turnaround Drive More Upside?
items.summary: Starbucks delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of positive comparable-store sales growth at 7.9%, with operating margins expanding 430 basis points to 14.4% and EPS increasing 70% to 85 cents. The company raised fiscal 2026 guidance, supported by improved customer traffic, menu innovation, and the revamped Rewards program. However, coffee cost pressures, potential store closures, and execution risks remain concerns.

items.title: Are Investors Undervaluing Occidental Petroleum (OXY) Right Now?
items.summary: Occidental Petroleum (OXY) is identified as an attractive value stock investment, holding a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating and an 'A' Value grade. The company's valuation metrics, including P/B ratio of 1.63, P/S ratio of 2.37, and P/CF ratio of 4.59, are all favorable compared to industry averages, suggesting the stock is undervalued with strong earnings outlook.

items.summary: Zacks analyzes five securities exchange stocks amid industry headwinds. The industry ranks #166 out of 247 Zacks industries with negative earnings outlook, having underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date. Five Hold-rated stocks are highlighted for consideration.

items.title: La Rosa Holdings Corp. to Change Its Name to Stratum Holdings Corp., Reflecting Its Transformation into an AI Infrastructure Company
items.summary: La Rosa Holdings Corp. is rebranding to Stratum Holdings Corp. effective October 19, 2026, with its stock ticker changing to SRTM on Nasdaq. The company is pivoting from real estate services to AI infrastructure, focusing on GPU leasing and high-performance compute after acquiring next-generation NVIDIA B300 GPUs under a long-term lease expected to generate recurring revenue.

items.title: FIS Stock Down Nearly 48% From 52-Week High: Is a Rebound Ahead?
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) has declined 48% from its 52-week high amid growth concerns, but improving cash flow and margin expansion offer recovery prospects. Second-quarter free cash flow surged 220% to $525 million, and the Global Payments Issuer Solutions acquisition is expected to add $700 million in free cash flow by 2028. However, lowered 2026 guidance for revenue growth (4.5-5%) and EBITDA growth (5.9-6.9%) highlight ongoing execution challenges. Recovery depends on translating integration benefits into sustainable margin gains and debt reduction rather than rapid revenue acceleration.

items.title: Truist Financial Corporation (TFC) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Miss Estimates
items.summary: Truist Financial reported Q3 earnings of $1.16 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $1.17, and revenues of $5.19 billion, falling short of expectations by 2.19%. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 18.5% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The company's industry, Banks - Major Regional, ranks in the bottom 33% of Zacks industries.

items.title: Citizens Financial Group (CFG) Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Citizens Financial Group reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.41 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.38, with a 2.17% earnings surprise. However, revenues of $2.32 billion slightly missed expectations. The stock has gained 8.6% year-to-date, underperforming the S&P 500's 13.1% gain. The company received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Better AI Stock: SpaceX vs. Nvidia
items.summary: Nvidia and SpaceX are compared as AI investment options. Nvidia, valued at $5.5 trillion, is a hardware play providing GPUs for AI workloads, while SpaceX, valued at $2 trillion, is an application play through its xAI subsidiary producing the Grok AI model. Despite SpaceX's faster growth, Nvidia is recommended as the better AI stock due to its established market dominance, doubling revenue, and significantly cheaper valuation relative to revenue.

items.title: This Dividend King Is Getting In on the AI Energy Boom With Its Recent Deal with Google. Is It a Buy?
items.summary: Black Hills, a Dividend King with 56 years of consecutive dividend growth, signed a long-term agreement with Google to supply 2.7 gigawatts of power to its Wyoming data center campus through 2048. The deal is projected to generate $150 million in annual net income by 2030, significantly boosting the utility's position as Wyoming emerges as a major AI data center hub with investments from Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet.

items.title: Billionaires Are Selling These 6 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks. Should You Follow?
items.summary: Several billionaire investors sold major AI stocks in Q2, including Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, citing concerns about AI infrastructure returns and valuations. However, the article advises against simply following these sales, recommending a company-by-company evaluation. Amazon and Apple are highlighted as top picks due to AWS growth and Apple's lower capex exposure to AI, while Tesla is flagged as overvalued given its unproven autonomous technology.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Over 45% of Berkshire Hathaway's $356 Billion Portfolio Invested in 3 Undeniable Winners
items.summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, has maintained the company's portfolio concentration strategy with over 45% ($160.6 billion) of invested assets in three major holdings: Apple ($76.73 billion), American Express ($46.72 billion), and Alphabet ($37.17 billion). While Buffett sold 75% of Apple before retirement, Abel views it as a long-term compounder. Abel has significantly increased Berkshire's Alphabet stake, tripling it in Q1 and adding $17 billion in Q2, attracted by Google's search dominance and AI ambitions in Google Cloud.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Just Shared Bad News for Nvidia and Great News for This Rival Chipmaker
items.summary: Microsoft plans to significantly expand its custom-designed Maia chips in Azure data centers starting next year, reducing reliance on Nvidia GPUs. The company will make Maia 300 chips its primary inference system for its products and services. This shift benefits Marvell Technology, which partners on the Maia chips, while pressuring Nvidia as major cloud providers develop custom AI accelerator alternatives.

items.title: Buy 5 Top-Ranked Non-Tech Nasdaq Stocks to Maximize Q4 Gains
items.summary: Despite the Nasdaq's tech-heavy composition, five non-tech Nasdaq-listed stocks with Zacks Rank #1 ratings are positioned for strong growth. Ross Stores plans 115 store openings with 13% Q2 sales growth, Roku's advertising revenue climbed 24.8%, APA Corp benefits from cost savings and long-term growth projects, Corcept Therapeutics sees strong drug demand with recent FDA approvals, and Halozyme generates royalties from pharma collaborations.

items.title: Sandisk Stock Could Be Worth $4,128 in the Next Year
items.summary: Sandisk stock has surged 497% year-to-date and could nearly triple to $4,128 over the next year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and data center storage growth. The company reported 51% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth to $9 billion, with CEO David Goeckeler stating the company is still in early innings of growth. Long-term customer agreements covering over half of fiscal 2027 bits shipped provide revenue visibility, though cyclical pricing risks remain.

items.title: Bill Ackman Is Directing Up to $3 Billion Into Howard Hughes' Insurance Arm, Vantage, as Part of His Plan to Build a Modern Berkshire Hathaway. Is HHH Stock the Way to Play His Buffett Ambitions?
items.summary: Bill Ackman is executing a plan to transform Howard Hughes Holdings (HHH) into a Berkshire Hathaway-style insurance holding company combined with an asset manager similar to Brookfield and Blackstone. HHH acquired Vantage for $2.1 billion and plans to invest $2.5-3 billion into the insurance unit over five years, with Pershing Square managing the portfolio. While the stock has pulled back to near book value after initial enthusiasm, the article cautions that success is uncertain and investors should wait for the excitement to subside before investing.

items.title: Sysco Reaches Agreement with Teamsters Locals 630 and 848 to End Strike
items.summary: Sysco Corporation announced it has reached a historic agreement with International Brotherhood of the Teamsters Locals 630 and 848, ending a strike at its Los Angeles facility. The company stated the agreement represents an important step toward restoring normal operations while maintaining service quality. Sysco emphasized the strike was not about wages or working conditions, and the company remains committed to providing colleagues with professional growth opportunities.

items.title: BULL Class Action Reminder - Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Webull Corporation Securities Fraud Class Action
items.summary: Robbins LLP is reminding investors of the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities fraud class action against Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL). The lawsuit alleges Webull falsely marketed itself as a U.S.-based company with isolated customer data, when in reality its operations, workforce, and infrastructure are structurally tied to China. The stock dropped 19% on October 7, 2026, after a U.S. House Select Committee report revealed the discrepancies, including that 62% of Webull's workforce operates in mainland China.

items.title: GOOGL Class Action Reminder: Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Alphabet Inc. Securities Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: Robbins LLP is reminding investors of the November 30, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities class action against Alphabet Inc. The lawsuit alleges that Alphabet failed to disclose that its Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model was delivering disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. The stock dropped 4.4% on July 16, 2026, when Bloomberg reported Google was months behind schedule on the flagship AI model.

items.title: DUOL Class Action Reminder - Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Duolingo, Inc. Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: Robbins LLP reminds investors of the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities fraud class action against Duolingo, Inc. The lawsuit alleges that Duolingo misled investors about product quality and sustainability by concealing negative impacts from aggressive monetization strategies and reliance on lower-quality AI-generated content. The company's stock declined significantly following three disclosure events in late 2025 and early 2026 that revealed slowing user growth and reduced profitability projections.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Cisco. This Is the AI Networking Stock Quietly Wiring Every Data Center
items.summary: Arista Networks is emerging as a critical AI infrastructure player by providing high-speed Ethernet switches that solve data center bottlenecks. As AI models grow more demanding, faster networking becomes essential to keep expensive GPUs operating at full capacity. Arista's stock has outperformed both Nvidia and Cisco this year, rising 54%, with strong Q2 results showing 37.7% revenue growth and guidance for continued expansion.

items.title: ROSEN, A LONGSTANDING FIRM, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action – APP
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed securities class action lawsuits against AppLovin Corporation, Lincoln Educational Services Corporation, and Beta Bionics, Inc. The AppLovin lawsuit alleges the company made false statements regarding AI video creative features and overstated the benefits of its AI models. Investors who purchased securities during specified class periods are encouraged to seek counsel before upcoming lead plaintiff deadlines.

items.title: Webull Corporation Class Action Lawsuit Seeks Recovery for Investors; December 7 2026, Deadline - Contact Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL) alleging material misstatements regarding the company's relationship with China. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased securities between April 26, 2025 and October 6, 2026. A CNBC report revealed that Webull's operations, ownership, and compliance infrastructure are heavily tied to China, contradicting its representation as an American company, causing the stock to drop 19% to $5.89 on October 7, 2026. The deadline to seek lead plaintiff status is December 7, 2026.

items.title: CoreWeave’s Debt Insurance Costs Just Hit a Record. Can It Keep Funding Its AI Boom?
items.summary: CoreWeave's credit default swap spreads hit a record 1,038 basis points, signaling market concerns about potential default. While the AI infrastructure company shows impressive growth with $2.58 billion in quarterly revenue and a $104 billion backlog, it carries $51 billion in debt and posted a negative $5.7 billion free cash flow last quarter. Rising borrowing costs could threaten the company's ability to fund its expansion if lenders become unwilling to extend more capital.

items.title: ROSEN, A GLOBAL AND LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Webull Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - BULL
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed multiple securities class action lawsuits against Webull Corporation, Alphabet Inc., and York Space Systems Inc., alleging false and misleading statements. The Webull lawsuit specifically claims the company misrepresented its operational independence from China, with core operations and data infrastructure tied to PRC-based personnel. Investors are encouraged to secure counsel before upcoming deadlines.

items.title: Arm vs. Credo Technology Group: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two semiconductor companies: Arm, which licenses chip architecture used in billions of devices globally with strong profitability and low risk, and Credo Technology Group, which provides high-speed interconnects for AI data centers with explosive 205% revenue growth but higher customer concentration risk. The author recommends Credo for its superior growth trajectory despite Arm's defensible business model.

items.title: Boeing Fell Back Below $200 Ahead of a Strike Deadline. Here's Why I'd Buy the Fear After New Contracts Were Signed
items.summary: Boeing stock has declined 11.3% over the past month and 26.7% from its 52-week high, but the author sees buying opportunity. The company averted a labor strike with 17,000 engineers and recently secured major defense contracts including development of next-generation carrier-based fighter jets and the F-47 to replace the F-15. Despite commercial aircraft challenges, the defense segment and government contract wins present potential upside.

items.title: Micron vs. NVIDIA: Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy After Earnings?
items.summary: Both Micron and NVIDIA have posted strong revenue growth and expanding margins driven by AI infrastructure demand. Micron's fiscal 2026 revenues reached $133.19 billion with a forward P/E of 5.18, while NVIDIA's Data Center revenues surged 117% to $89 billion with a forward P/E of 23.93. Despite NVIDIA's impressive growth, Micron is positioned as the more compelling buy due to its lower financial leverage (3.3% debt-to-equity vs NVIDIA's 14.1%), more attractive valuation, and potential for sustained growth as it evolves into a vital AI infrastructure supplier.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro's performance. The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, and that management's positive statements about the company's business and prospects lacked a reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.title: Innodata Stock's Premium Valuation: Can AI Growth Justify the Price?
items.summary: Innodata (INOD) trades at a premium 35.47X forward P/E ratio despite a 34.3% stock decline over the past year. While the company benefits from strong AI demand with Q2 revenues surging 58% to $92.1 million and adjusted EBITDA jumping 92%, concerns about customer concentration (top two customers represent 71% of revenues), margin volatility, and downward 2027 earnings revisions warrant caution. The stock receives a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting investors await better entry points.

items.title: Stock Market Midday, Oct. 15: Markets Mixed as AI Sell-Off Continues
items.summary: Markets showed mixed performance on October 15, 2026, as concerns over AI debt and capital costs triggered a semiconductor sell-off. The Dow rose 0.82% while the Nasdaq fell 0.36%. Inflation data and CoreWeave's elevated bond yields (15%) spooked investors, though Nvidia's CEO attempted to restore confidence. AI stocks comprise 40% of the S&P 500, making diversification critical for investors.

items.title: This Warning Signal Just Flashed Ahead of Netflix's Earnings -- Here's What It Means for the Stock
items.summary: Netflix announced a 6% workforce reduction (approximately 1,000 workers) ahead of its third-quarter 2026 earnings report on October 20. The company's statement that it remains 'on track' to deliver forecasts—rather than exceeding them—suggests no surprise earnings beats are expected. Combined with CEO comments about slower-than-desired growth and a 24.7% stock price decline year-to-date, the article suggests investors wait for evidence of subscriber engagement improvements and meaningful revenue growth from new ventures like live sports before investing.

items.title: Prologis' Q3 FFO Beat Estimates as Rental Revenues Rise
items.summary: Prologis (PLD) reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $1.60 per share, up 7.4% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates. Rental revenues grew 7.4% to $2.21B, while average occupancy improved to 95.1%. The company narrowed 2026 core FFO guidance to $6.25-$6.29 and raised development starts guidance to $5.0-$5.75B, reflecting strong operational performance and capital deployment plans.

items.title: JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Which Stock Has the Edge After Q3 Results?
items.summary: JPMorgan and Citigroup reported Q3 earnings with contrasting profiles. JPMorgan demonstrated earnings resilience with 6% net income growth, benefiting from higher net interest income and loan growth, while maintaining industry-leading profitability and a strong balance sheet. Citigroup delivered robust 40% net income growth as its multiyear restructuring gains momentum, with improved efficiency ratios and cost discipline. JPMorgan trades at a premium valuation (13.41X forward P/E) reflecting its stability, while Citigroup's discounted valuation (9.74X) presents greater upside potential if its turnaround succeeds. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Expand Energy Stock Declines 17% YTD: How Should Investors Play It?
items.summary: Expand Energy (EXE), the largest U.S. independent natural gas producer formed from the Chesapeake-Southwestern merger, has underperformed its sector by 17.4% YTD despite projected 40.8% earnings growth in 2026. While the company benefits from a discounted valuation, the $1.25B Twin Eagle acquisition, and strong balance sheet improvements, significant headwinds including natural gas price volatility, high capital expenditures ($2.75-2.95B), rising transportation costs, and integration risks warrant a cautious Hold rating.

items.title: Better Artificial Intelligence Stock for 2026: Astera Labs vs. Marvell Technology
items.summary: The article compares two semiconductor companies powering AI data centers: Astera Labs, a high-speed connectivity specialist with 115% revenue growth but high customer concentration (70% from one customer), and Marvell Technology, a broader semiconductor provider with 42% growth, lower valuation multiples, and confidence in reaching $70-90 billion in revenue by 2031. The author recommends Marvell due to its more attractive valuation, diversified product portfolio, and long-term growth visibility despite both companies facing customer concentration and geopolitical risks.

items.title: SEC Approves HOOD-Linked KPI Contracts: A New Growth Avenue Unlocked?
items.summary: The SEC approved Cboe Global Markets' proposal to list binary options tied to company-specific KPIs, with Robinhood Markets expected to become the first retail brokerage offering these contracts covering over 100 metrics across 23 companies. While this presents a new revenue opportunity aligned with Robinhood's active-trading strategy, near-term monetization is limited by pending clearing approvals and fee waivers through 2026. Regulatory uncertainty around event-driven products and the need for sustained customer adoption also present challenges.

items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. and certain officers for alleged securities law violations. items.title: VEOEY or WM: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two waste removal services stocks, Veolia Environnement SA (VEOEY) emerges as the better value option compared to Waste Management (WM). items.title: Figma vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Figma and Palantir Technologies as investment options in 2026. Palantir is recommended as the stronger choice, posting 150% U.S. commercial revenue growth in Q2 2026 with profitability and raised guidance, while Figma, despite strong revenue growth, saw its stock drop 16% after earnings due to heavy AI investment costs compressing margins and widening operating losses.

items.title: CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Credo Technology (CRDO) and Coherent Corp (COHR) are both capitalizing on AI data center expansion through different approaches. CRDO specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions with forecasted 85%+ revenue growth by FY2027, while COHR manufactures optical components and targets $3B+ quarterly revenues by FY2027-end. COHR receives a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating versus CRDO's #3 (Hold), with COHR considered the better pick despite higher capital expenditure pressures.

items.title: Morgan Stanley Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Wealth and AI Strategy
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 2026 EPS of $3.03 on $20.34B in revenues, beating estimates. The firm achieved record Wealth Management revenues of $9.1B with $232B in net new assets. Management highlighted AI infrastructure financing as a major growth opportunity and targets further margin expansion, while acknowledging risks from elevated interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: BNY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Fee Income & NII Growth
items.summary: Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.37, beating consensus estimates of $2.26, with a 24.1% year-over-year increase. Total revenues rose 11.7% to $5.68B, driven by higher fee revenues and net interest income. However, the company faces headwinds from rising expenses, deposit margin compression, and net outflows in assets under management. Capital ratios declined compared to the prior year.

items.title: MMM Q3 Earnings on Deck: How to Approach the Stock Now?
items.summary: 3M is expected to report Q3 2026 revenue of $6.60 billion and EPS of $2.41 on October 20. However, weakness in the Consumer segment and elevated R&D costs pose challenges. The stock trades at a premium valuation compared to industry peers.

items.title: Archer Daniels' Sweetener Weakness: Can Ethanol Offset It?
items.summary: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) reported a 22% year-over-year increase in Carbohydrate Solutions operating profit to $411 million in Q2 2026, driven by strong ethanol margins and policy incentives that offset weakness in liquid sweeteners. ADM raised its expected 2026 benefit from the 45Z policy to $250 million from $150 million, supporting its outlook despite ongoing challenges in North American sweetener volumes.

items.summary: As AI adoption shifts from infrastructure building to productivity gains, Synopsys emerges as a potential winner by providing chip design software and IP. items.title: HPQ Jumps 37% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: HP Inc. (HPQ) has gained 36.7% year-to-date and trades at a significant valuation discount with a forward P/S ratio of 0.46 versus industry average of 8.58. The company is benefiting from AI PC adoption (46% of Personal Systems shipments), strong revenue growth in premium products (18.5% YTD despite declining unit volumes), and consistent Industrial Printing growth. HPQ received a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating based on product innovation, premiumization strategy, and attractive valuation metrics.

items.title: Can Gaming Pipeline and Activision Add Momentum to Microsoft Stock?
items.summary: Microsoft is betting on major fall gaming releases, including Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, to revive its struggling Xbox business. However, near-term guidance shows Xbox content and services revenues expected to decline in mid-single digits through Q1 fiscal 2027, with hardware also falling year-over-year. The company expects recovery in fiscal 2027 as it resets its portfolio. Competitors Take-Two and Roblox face similar uneven gaming trends, with both showing near-term headwinds despite long-term growth catalysts.

items.title: Block's AI-Powered Kiosk Launch to Drive Revenue and Merchant Growth
items.summary: Block, Inc. has introduced Square Kiosk, an AI-powered self-service ordering system designed for quick-service restaurants. The kiosk features a 21.5-inch touchscreen, conversational AI voice capabilities, integrated payments, and personalized loyalty features. Priced at $1,999 with a $99 monthly software fee, the product aims to streamline ordering, improve customer experiences, and increase transaction values through intelligent add-on suggestions. The launch is expected to strengthen Block's position in restaurant technology and support revenue growth through hardware sales, recurring software fees, and increased payment processing volumes.

items.title: Wells Fargo Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Interest Income Outlook
items.summary: Wells Fargo reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.87 per share, beating consensus estimates, and reaffirmed full-year net interest income guidance of $50 billion. The bank highlighted deposit growth of 11% to $1.48 trillion, a 16.3% return on tangible common equity approaching its 17-18% target, and continued consumer lending expansion. However, Markets revenues declined 1% year-over-year due to trading volatility, and the company faces headwinds from sustained higher rates and inflation.

items.title: S&P 500 ETFs Defy Rate Worries as Earnings Outlook Strengthens
items.summary: The S&P 500 has demonstrated remarkable resilience with a 52-day streak without a 1% decline and 224 consecutive NYSE sessions without broad-based selling. Strong earnings expectations (24.3% Q3 growth) and positive estimate revisions support market confidence despite inflation, hawkish Fed policy, and midterm election uncertainty. Historical data shows positive returns in the 12 months following midterm elections, while holiday retail sales are projected to reach record levels.

Despite heavy capex spending and reliance on investment gains, the company maintains positive free cash flow, growing Google Cloud revenue, and competitive AI capabilities through Gemini and Waymo.

items.title: TSLA's Megapack Order Highlights AI Demand and Future Growth Potential

Tesla's energy storage business continues to grow with 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026, but the company faces competition from Fluence Energy and Bloom Energy in the AI infrastructure power market.

items.summary: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta are projected to spend $745 billion on capital expenditures this year, primarily for data center infrastructure. Hardware suppliers Nvidia, Broadcom, and Arista Networks are positioned to benefit from this spending through GPU sales, custom AI chips, and networking equipment. Nvidia trades at an attractive 14x forward P/E, Broadcom at 18x with strong AI revenue growth projections, while Arista commands a premium 38x valuation despite deployment risks.

items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. for allegedly making false statements and failing to disclose that it shares consumers' health information with third-party advertising platforms and charges for prescriptions immediately after intake forms are submitted. The FTC, California, and Utah filed a separate lawsuit on July 29, 2026, resulting in a 14.73% stock price decline.

items.title: Can AI Products and Automation Drive WTW's Growth and Higher Margins?
items.summary: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) is expanding AI-driven insurance technology capabilities through platforms like RiskIQ Nexus and Radar AI Assistant to improve risk management and underwriting. The company's Propel AI program targets $400 million in annualized savings by 2028, with $350 million retained after reinvestment. WTW aims for a 30% adjusted operating margin by 2028, though implementation costs and adoption risks remain concerns. The stock trades at a lower P/E multiple than peers and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Meta Platforms Rises 12% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Meta Platforms shares gained 12.4% over three months, driven by robust advertising demand and AI-powered engagement. Q2 ad revenues surged 27% to $59.4 billion with Advantage+ solutions exceeding a $75 billion annual run rate. However, the company faces margin pressure as Q2 expenses jumped 55% and 2026 capital spending may reach $145 billion. Despite strong AI capabilities and expanding Muse portfolio, rising infrastructure costs and stiff competition from other AI agents remain headwinds.

items.title: The First Pure-Play Humanoid Robot Stock Is About to Go Public. Here's What Investors Need to Know About Agility Robotics.
items.summary: Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid robot, is going public through a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI at a $2.5 billion valuation. While the company has impressive technology and $300 million in orders, it lost $140 million on only $1.8 million in sales last year. The stock is expected to be highly volatile as investors debate whether humanoid robots will mainstream within weeks or take a decade, with most tech IPOs declining in their first months after going public.

items.title: IREN's Global Expansion Accelerates: Can It Drive Future Growth?
items.summary: IREN Limited is expanding its AI data center infrastructure globally with a 5GW development pipeline across North America, Europe, and Australia. The company targets 300MW of commissioned capacity by end-2026 and 800MW by end-2027, with $4 billion in contracted annualized revenues. However, the company faces significant capital expenditure requirements of $25-30 billion for fiscal 2027 and has seen recent stock underperformance with downward earnings revisions.

items.title: Kinder Morgan Restores US-Mexico Gas Flows After Pipeline Outage
items.summary: Kinder Morgan (KMI) has resumed natural gas deliveries to Mexico through its Tennessee Gas Pipeline following infrastructure repairs. The company lifted its force majeure declaration after resolving operational issues affecting cross-border shipments. Mexico's heavy reliance on U.S. natural gas imports for electricity generation and industrial use supports steady demand for KMI's transportation services.

items.title: Kraft Heinz vs. Coca-Cola: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Kraft Heinz and Coca-Cola represent different investment strategies in the consumer staples sector. Kraft Heinz trades at a steep discount (11x forward P/E) with a high 7.2% dividend yield but faces profitability challenges, a $9.3B impairment charge, and declining margins. Coca-Cola commands a premium valuation (27x forward P/E) justified by superior 27.3% net margins, consistent profitability, and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases. The article suggests Kraft Heinz may appeal more to deep-value investors despite turnaround risks, while Coca-Cola offers stability and proven cash generation.

items.title: Intuit vs. Oracle: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Intuit and Oracle as investment options in 2026. Intuit trades at cheaper valuations but faces intense competition from low-cost alternatives and fintech startups in the tax software space. Oracle shows stronger growth momentum with 30% year-over-year cloud revenue growth and a large backlog of contracted services, though it carries higher debt levels. The author recommends Oracle over Intuit, citing Oracle's positioning in the growing AI infrastructure market versus Intuit's vulnerability to competitive moat erosion.

items.title: JPM Q3 Earnings Lag on Lower Fixed Income Markets, IB Offer Support

Management raised its 2026 NII outlook to $106.2 billion but also increased expense guidance to $108.6 billion.

items.title: Quantum Builds ActiveScale Momentum: Can It Sustain Growth?
items.summary: Quantum Corporation (QMCO) reported 26% revenue growth to $80.8 million, driven by strong demand for its ActiveScale object storage platform and tape solutions. The company secured major deals including an $80+ million APAC hyperscaler deployment and a European biometrics renewal. However, disk drive and tape component shortages limit fulfillment capacity, and competition from IBM and NetApp in the AI-ready storage market poses risks to sustained growth.

items.title: Eightfold AI welcomes Joe Korngiebel as CEO to lead its next chapter of growth

items.title: Coca-Cola vs. PepsiCo: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo present different investment profiles for 2026. Coca-Cola offers superior profitability with a 27.3% net margin and strong historical returns (92% over 5 years), but trades at a premium valuation (27x P/E). PepsiCo provides better value with a lower P/E ratio (15x), higher dividend yield (4.6%), and diversified food/beverage portfolio, but faces commodity pressures and lower profitability margins (8.8% net margin). The choice depends on investor priorities: growth and profitability favor Coca-Cola, while value and income favor PepsiCo.

items.title: Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
items.summary: Dell Technologies has gained 8% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's 2.1% return. items.summary: A $10,000 investment split evenly between Alphabet and Nvidia could grow to $17,245-$28,785 by 2030. Both companies are positioned at the forefront of AI, quantum computing, and autonomous vehicles.

items.summary: Lumentum stock fell 9.8% on Monday following cautionary comments from Broadcom CEO Hock Tan over the weekend. Tan suggested many investors don't understand their AI investments and compared enterprise AI token usage to a 'casino,' questioning whether current AI spending will lead to sustainable, profitable business models. This sparked a broader pullback in AI infrastructure stocks, hitting Lumentum particularly hard after it surged to all-time highs the previous week when its CEO announced near sell-out status through 2029.

items.title: Boeing vs. GE Aerospace: Which U.S. Industrial Giant's Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: GE Aerospace emerges as the better investment choice in 2026 compared to Boeing. GE Aerospace, conversely, demonstrates strong fundamentals with a 19% net margin, $7.3 billion in free cash flow, and a more reasonable valuation multiple, supported by recent major contracts from airlines and the U.S. military.

items.title: Does Fortinet's Strong Margin Profile Make the Stock Worth Buying Now?
items.summary: Fortinet achieved record non-GAAP operating margins of 38% in Q2 2026 with strong free cash flow of $966M, raising full-year margin and EPS guidance. The complaint claims the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked credible evidence of execution, and that revenue targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are eligible to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.summary: Alibaba announced plans to build over 20 gigawatts of global data center capacity by 2032 and unveiled its Zhenwu V900 AI chip. The key question remains whether aggressive AI spending will deliver on its three-year payback targets.

items.title: UAL Strengthens FTAI Partnership With Expanded Engine Exchange Program
items.summary: United Airlines has expanded its partnership with FTAI Aviation Ltd. to include an engine exchange program for CFM56-7B engines on its Boeing 737 NG fleet. The multi-year agreement aims to reduce aircraft downtime, improve fleet utilization, and stabilize maintenance costs. FTAI will acquire unserviceable engines for its MRO network while supplying serviceable replacements, creating growth opportunities for both companies, though FTAI's financial benefits will depend on contract margins and refurbishment costs.

items.title: Can AI Drive Refining Efficiency & Profits for Phillips 66?
items.summary: Phillips 66, Chevron, and Shell are increasingly deploying artificial intelligence and machine learning across their operations to improve refinery efficiency, optimize maintenance, and reduce costs. Phillips 66 has achieved over $1 per barrel in cost savings and targets $1.50 per barrel, with AI enabling problem-solving in days or weeks rather than months. While AI benefits remain partially unquantified, these initiatives are expected to strengthen long-term profitability and operational performance.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase's Next Earnings Report Tomorrow Could Send the Stock Plunging. Here's Why.
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase's Q3 earnings report could trigger a stock decline due to rising bond yields pressuring bank stocks. While the bank expects solid investment banking and trading revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens, investors have set a high bar and may react negatively to any missed estimates, weakened guidance, or signs of deteriorating credit quality. Rising yields increase funding costs and borrowing expenses, potentially slowing lending and investment banking activity.

items.title: CVX Outpaces Industry in Past 6 Months: Should Investors Stay Bullish?
items.summary: Chevron (CVX) has outperformed its sub-industry and broader energy sector over the past six months, gaining 10.6%. items.title: Why ExxonMobil's Venezuela Warning Could Matter for Energy Investors Right Now
items.summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods initially called Venezuela 'uninvestable,' but the company is now reportedly in talks to invest in Venezuelan oilfields. However, Venezuela's production capacity remains severely constrained at 1.2 million barrels per day versus its historical peak of 3.5 million, meaning any investment there won't materially impact global oil prices in the near term. For ExxonMobil investors, Venezuela represents a potential bonus rather than a core growth driver, with the company's primary growth engines being its operations in Guyana and the Permian Basin.

items.summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway held Wells Fargo stock for nearly 30 years starting in 1989, but exited the position in 2022 following the bank's 2016 phony accounts scandal. While CEO Charlie Scharf successfully turned the bank around with operational improvements and regulatory compliance, Buffett had already sold due to frustration with the board and uncertainty about the turnaround timeline. The case illustrates the importance of reputation in banking and the challenge of identifying viable long-term turnaround opportunities.

items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported disappointing Q3 results, missing earnings and revenue expectations despite record revenue and strong travel demand. items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.72 per share, missing estimates by 4.44% as fuel costs surged 62%. items.summary: The article compares two specialized hardware companies: Cerebras Systems, which builds AI-accelerating wafer-scale processors and recently achieved profitability with $510M revenue but faces competitive pressure from Nvidia; and IonQ, a quantum computing leader with 202% revenue growth to $130M but still unprofitable with $510M net losses. items.summary: Nvidia and Broadcom are positioned for significant growth through 2028, with both companies forecasting substantial revenue increases driven by AI infrastructure demand. Based on these growth trajectories and historical valuations, an equal investment in both stocks could potentially triple by 2028.

items.summary: While AMD has outperformed Nvidia in 2026 with a 200% rise versus Nvidia's 30%, the article argues Nvidia offers greater future upside. AMD's valuation has become stretched with its forward P/E ratio surging, and despite strong data center growth of 107%, it lags Nvidia's 117% growth. Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chip architecture and projected 70% revenue growth in 2027 position it as the better investment despite being the world's largest company.

However, elevated valuation at 34.79X forward P/E (above industry average of 27.16X), rising debt levels of $19.2 billion, and surging costs present risks. items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings expectations with 3.1% organic revenue growth and a 3.7% stock price increase, despite cutting full-year EPS guidance to 2.5%-3.5%. The company faces challenges in North America beverages and snacks due to GLP-1 drug impacts and consumer pushback, but international segments remain strong. With a 4.6% dividend yield and P/E of 15, the stock may appeal to defensive dividend investors seeking recovery potential.

items.title: SPCX to Acquire 800 MHz Spectrum for Superior Network: Buy the Stock?
items.summary: SpaceX has agreed to acquire Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum portfolio to enhance Starlink Mobile's connectivity capabilities. The low-band spectrum will enable a hybrid satellite-terrestrial network, improving indoor coverage and reliability. Combined with previously acquired 2 GHz spectrum from EchoStar, this positions SpaceX to compete as a major U.S. wireless operator while expanding its AI infrastructure ambitions.

items.title: 3 Top-Ranked Stocks Breaking Records on AI-Related Demand
items.summary: Micron, NVIDIA, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise have all posted stellar quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand. items.title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Microsoft, Dell, HP, Lenovo and Nvidia
items.summary: Microsoft expanded its partnership with Nvidia, launching AI-powered Surface Laptop Ultra ($2,599) and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box ($5,999) to enable on-device AI processing. items.title: Nebius Group vs. SoundHound AI: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Nebius Group and SoundHound AI represent different plays in the AI infrastructure boom. Nebius operates a specialized cloud platform for AI workloads with 350% revenue growth and demand exceeding supply, while SoundHound AI provides voice-enabled software with 99% revenue growth but faces profitability challenges and integration risks. The author recommends Nebius due to its stronger market position and less competitive landscape.

items.title: BigBear.ai vs. Nebius: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two AI-focused tech stocks with opposite market approaches. BigBear.ai provides defense and government intelligence software but faces declining revenue (down 19% in 2025) and mounting losses ($294M net loss). Nebius Group operates AI cloud infrastructure with explosive 479% revenue growth in 2025 and positive net income of $82M, though it carries massive negative free cash flow due to capital-intensive GPU infrastructure spending. The author recommends Nebius as the better buy, citing its larger addressable market ($1 trillion GPU cloud opportunity), consistent profitability, and superior growth trajectory compared to BigBear.ai's struggling government contract model.

items.title: ROSEN, LEADING INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Duolingo, Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased Class A common stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Duolingo made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates, failed to disclose that increased user friction from ads and subscription upsells was negatively impacting DAU growth, and concealed that AI-generated content was degrading product quality and user experience. items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings expectations but lowered full-year guidance, citing North American weakness and margin pressures. Despite attractive valuation and higher dividend yield, PEP significantly underperformed Coca-Cola year-to-date. items.title: AbbVie's Temab-A Gets Two FDA Breakthrough Therapy Tags in Cancer
items.summary: AbbVie announced that its investigational antibody-drug conjugate Temab-A (telisotuzumab adizutecan) has received two FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. The designations were based on data from the M21-404 study, and the company is evaluating Temab-A across multiple advanced solid tumors as part of its expanding oncology pipeline.

items.summary: A comparison of two restaurant stocks shows Yum China Holdings (YUMC) as the superior value option compared to Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG). items.summary: Applied Digital has secured $36 billion in contracted AI data center revenue, but most capacity still needs to be built. items.title: Best Buy's Ads & Marketplace Expansion Opens New Growth Opportunities
items.summary: Best Buy is expanding its advertising and marketplace businesses to create additional profit streams and improve margins. Best Buy Ads targets 10% collections growth in fiscal 2027 on $900 million in prior-year collections, while Marketplace GMV outlook was raised to $1.3 billion after strong Q2 results. items.title: Jensen Huang Has Dismissed AI "Doomsday Narratives," Saying, "Scaring People Is Unnecessary. It Is Irresponsible." Here's Why That Stance Matters for Nvidia's Growth Story.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed concerns about AI risks and development slowdowns, stating that fears are overblown and that 2030 will not be 'the end of the world.' While some AI leaders like Anthropic's Dario Amodei have called for slower development, Huang argues that safe deployment of AI products directly benefits Nvidia's long-term value. Despite initial stock declines following AI safety warnings, Nvidia has recovered and hit new highs, with Wall Street expecting 91% year-over-year revenue growth.

items.title: Can Microsoft's Big AI Capex Translate Into Sustainable Returns Ahead?

items.title: Prediction: Johnson & Johnson Will Be a Faster-Growing Company by 2030 Than Most Investors Expect
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson is positioned for faster growth by 2030 following its separation from its slower-growing consumer health division. The company can now focus investments on its faster-growing biopharma and medtech segments. Key growth drivers include recent drug approvals like ICOTYDE and the FDA-cleared Ottava robotic surgery system, which operates in a market with significant expansion potential. Despite challenges from government price negotiations and talc-related lawsuits, J&J's diversified portfolio and strong dividend history make it an attractive long-term investment.

items.summary: SpaceX launched a test satellite with Google's TPUs to explore orbital data centers, but satellite-based data centers will cost 2.5-3x more than Earth-based facilities. Tech giants need computing power immediately and are investing heavily in neocloud companies like Nebius and Iren, which have available megawatt capacity and scaling pipelines. Orbital data centers are unlikely to replace terrestrial data centers in the near term.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Through 2030, It Would be This One.
items.summary: While Nvidia and Micron dominate AI chip headlines, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is positioned as the superior long-term AI infrastructure play. Despite the integration, Cardano has only recorded 38,777 transactions compared to competitors Base (85M) and Solana (66.9M), and even if it captured all x402 payments, the revenue would represent only a small fraction of its market cap. Transaction fees have also declined significantly year-over-year.

items.title: Greg Abel-Led Berkshire Hathaway Owns 3 Consumer Stocks. Here's the One I'd Buy First.
items.summary: Among Berkshire Hathaway's three main consumer staples holdings, Kroger emerges as the most attractive buy opportunity. While Coca-Cola remains the best quality company but has become expensive, and Kraft Heinz is distracted by restructuring plans, Kroger's recent pullback from March highs has created an attractive entry point. New CEO Greg Foran's price-cutting strategy is working to improve competitiveness, and the company maintains strong dividend growth with 20 consecutive years of increases and aggressive share buybacks.

items.title: Meta's Muse AI: Good or Bad for E-Commerce? Shopify and Amazon Are Taking Opposite Approaches.

Amazon's logistics network, customer data, and Prime loyalty program provide competitive advantages that could mitigate threats from agentic AI shopping.

items.title: ASML vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company: What Revenue Trends Tell Investors About These Companies Tied to Artificial Intelligence
